text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Nottingham Forest and Arsenal at The City Ground!

Forest were on a run of seven without a win (D1 L6) before Nuno Espirito Santo took over, with the Portuguese since overseeing just one loss in his six games at the helm (W3 D2), though that did come in their last Premier League outing when they were beaten 3-2 by Brentford.
After seeing a flurry of goals in the first five games under Nuno, Forest played out a 0-0 draw away at Bristol City in their last match in the FA Cup, forcing them to another replay.

It was a 1-0 defeat in this exact fixture last season that ended Arsenal's title hopes, and the Gunners will be looking to avoid a similar scoreline here as they look to close the gap to Liverpool at the top of the table.

They had a slight wobble before their mid-season break, winning just one of their seven games in all competitions (D3 L3), but came back revitalised with a thumping 5-0 win over Crystal Palace last time out.
However, they're winless in their last three Premier League away games (D1 L2) and haven't won any of their last three trips to The City Ground in all competitions.
Nuno makes three changes from the side that drew with Bristol on Friday, as Toffolo, Gibbs-White and Williams are all brought in.
Mangala retains his place, despite reports linking him with a possible move to Lyon today.
Yates and Hudson-Odoi drop to the bench, where they are boosted by the returns of Felipe, Elanga and Awoniyi from injury.
Nuno Tavares is ineligible to face his parent club.
Mikel Arteta makes just two changes to the side that beat Palace last time out.
Smith Rowe and Martinelli, who scored twice after coming off the bench in that game, both come in.
Gabriel and Rice are also fit to start after passing late fitness checks following respective ankle and thigh problems.
Havertz and Trossard start on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Odegaard gets the game under way for Arsenal!
Forest crowd bodies down their left side, forcing Arsenal to switch it out to the opposite flank.
Jesus plays a one-two with Martinelli to try and open up space on the edge of the box, but he can't get a sight of goal.
Jesus has started the game out on the left for the Gunners and he floats a cross into the box.
It's just too high for Smith Rowe to get his head on, and Turner plucks it out of the air.
Forest are starting to press higher upfield now, and they're forcing Arsenal deeper into their own half.
Gabriel just squeezes his pass past a stretching Williams, but Martinelli doesn't get too far with Dominguez tight to him.
Arsenal have won five of their last six Premier League games against Forest (L1), and are looking to do the double over them in the competition for just the second time (also in 1998-99).
Saka darts in behind down the right, but there's barely any space in the Forest penalty area.
He tries to pull it back to the byline, but there are three red shirts between him and his closest team-mate.
Forest are struggling to get a foothold in the game so far, with Arsenal quickly winning it back whenever possession is turned over.
The hosts are defending in numbers though, making things difficult for the Gunners.
BLOCK! Odegaard sees a low shot blocked from the right, and Arsenal quickly switch it out to the opposite flank, with Martinelli sliding it through for Smith Rowe.
He squares it into the middle for Jesus, but his first-time shot deflects over off Omobamidele.
The offside flag goes up to end an Arsenal attack, and now there's a break in play, Turner goes down holding his right hand.
He needs treatment, but he's quickly back on his feet to continue.
Forest's first push into the final third is quickly smothered, and Arsenal break quickly on the counter.
Zinchenko tries to slide in Jesus on the left of the box, but the offside flag is up once more.
Raya goes long with a free-kick, and White gets in front of Toffolo down the right.
A heavy touch at the wrong moment gets away from him though, and he runs it out of play before he can put a cross in.
Arsenal have had 71 per cent possession so far in this game, and they don't look like letting up the pressure any time soon.
Martinelli drops a shoulder to lose Montiel down the right, but there are no Arsenal players in the box to get on the end of his cross.
Jesus drops deep in his own half to cut out a Forest attack before setting Martinelli on the break.
He drives down the left and sees a cross blocked by Williams, who goes to ground.
He's holding his wrist, but he gets back up without needing treatment.
Williams is penalised for a handball in midfield and Arsenal win a free-kick.
After some debate, it's Odegaard that whips it into the box, but Turner rushes off his line to collect it.
Martinelli is getting a lot of joy down the left, and after Rice stops Gibbs-White's cross, he sets the Brazilian on his way.
He fizzes a low cross into the box this time, but Murillo slides in to stop it from reaching Saka.
Saka gets a yard on Toffolo and lays it off to Odegaard, who touches it straight to Jesus.
Instead of turning to have a shot, he tries to return it to the Arsenal captain, but it's one pass too many, and Forest clear their lines.
CHANCE! It's better from Arsenal here as Jesus slips away from Williams to burst along the edge of the box before touching it into Smith Rowe's feet.
He spins to get a shot away, but he scoops it just wide of the near post.
Forest have barely managed a touch of the ball in the last five minutes as Arsenal continue to up the pressure.
Jesus is in the middle of every attack as he lifts it over the top towards Martinelli, but Omabamidele stretches to nod it out of his path.
The Forest fans aren't happy with the referee at the moment, as they feel they should've had a free-kick.
Dominguez looks to play a one-two with Williams, but he's blocked off from getting to the return pass.
The referee waves him back to his feet.
BLOCK! There's a collision between Omabamidele and Montiel that sees the latter stay down in the box, but the referee doesn't stop play as it isn't a head injury.
Martinelli carries on, curling a shot on goal, but it's blocked by Murillo.
Now that the danger has gone for Forest, Montiel goes down once more.
He was caught on his shoulder by Omabamidele's studs and needs treatment.
He's okay to carry on.
Again, Arsenal overwork it in the final third, and another chance goes begging.
It's more good work by Jesus down the left as he fizzes it into the box, but Odegaard chooses to knock it onto Rice.
There isn't enough on it though, and Danilo pokes it away.
Jesus picks up the first yellow card of the game.
He's complaining about a decision not going his way and gets booked for dissent.
CHANCE! Danilo wins it back in midfield and the space just opens up in front of him to drive into.
He takes it to the edge of the D before taking aim, but his shot sails just over Raya's crossbar.
SO CLOSE! Zinchenko's sliced cross isn't dealt with by Forest, and Smith Rowe keeps the move alive for Arsenal.
His touch is heavy, but it ends up being a good pass to Saka, whose first-time shot trickles just wide of the near post after taking a deflection off Murillo.
Into the first of three added minutes, and Arsenal are trying to get a goal just before the break.
They're still finding a lot of space down their left, with Zinchenko clipping it in this time, but Jesus' header loops high over the bar.
GOOD SAVE! In the final action of the first half, Saka checks back to lose Montiel before curling a deep cross into the far post.
Jesus gets above Omabamidele to head it towards the top corner, but Turner stretches to tip it over.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-0 ARSENAL.
Despite Arsenal's dominance over Forest in the first half, it's goalless at the break.
The Gunners had 81 per cent possession but struggled to break down a compact Forest side in front of them.
Their best chance came on the stroke of half-time as Jesus' header had to be scrambled over by Turner, with Smith Rowe also sending an attempt over on the half-hour mark.
Forest barely got out of their own half, but Danilo had a good chance, only to send it over the bar when one-on-one with Raya.
As soon as the half-time whistle blew, Arteta set off on a jog down the tunnel, clearly eager to get his team inside.
Everything has worked for them until they got it into the final third, and they need to come up with a plan on how to open up their opponents.
Forest have defended as a unit, which Nuno will have been pleased to see.
They'll likely keep biding their time, looking for the golden chance that could snatch something from this game.
There's a change at the break for Forest, and it's a straight swap up front.
Wood struggled to get into the game, and he's replaced by Awoniyi.
Forest get us back under way for the second half!
Arsenal have picked up where they left off in the first half, with Saka linking up well with Jesus down the right.
The Brazilian fizzes a low cross towards Smith Rowe, but Murillo hooks it away.
Zinchenko chips it forward for Martinelli, and it looks like the chance is gone when he trips, but he does well to still get a cross away.
He can't pick out a team-mate either though, and Forest clear their lines once more.
Gibbs-White tries to pick out Awoniyi with an early pass, but Gabriel blocks it, only to gift possession back to the midfielder.

source.text: Gibbs-White tries to pick out Awoniyi

text: He switches it out to Williams on the right instead, but Saliba gets in the way of that cross.
That's much better by Forest!
SAVE! Awoniyi is wrestled down by Saliba to win a free-kick, and Gibbs-White curls a good delivery into the box.
Williams rises highest to nod it towards goal, but it's straight down the middle at Raya.
GREAT SAVE! The game has opened up in the last couple of minutes, and Arsenal surge forward on the counter.
It's not the cleanest strike by Saka as it bobbles in front of him and takes a slight nick off Montiel, but Turner still needs to get a strong arm behind it.
Jesus has his hands up at the far post, asking for Martinelli to pick him out as he's completely unmarked.
His fellow Brazilian tries to do just that, but Murillo thumps it away for a corner in front of Turner, who had it covered.
OFF THE POST! It's great play from Arsenal, as Saka rolls it back to Odegaard, who dummies a shot before laying it off to Jesus on the right of the box.
He's one-on-one with Turner and rifles a powerful shot past him, but it ricochets off the near post.

events.action: rifles a powerful shot past him

text: Forest have only won one of their last six Premier League games when drawing 0-0 at half-time (D3 L2), although that win did come in their most recent such match (2-1 v Manchester United in December).
Danilo spins away from two Arsenal defenders with clever turns, hooking the ball over his shoulder each time.
There are half-hearted shouts from the stands for a penalty after he goes down under pressure from Gabriel in the box, but nothing's given.
Omabamidele darts in front of Smith Rowe to cut out Martinelli's cross, only to gift it straight back to the winger.
He tries to pick out Jesus with his second attempt, but Danilo intercepts that one.

text: Forest are making another change here, and it's another adjustment to their frontline.
Dominguez goes off, with Hudson-Odoi brought on in his place.
JESUS SCORES! Arsenal finally break the deadlock! After all of their hard work, Forest are opened up by a long throw-in from Zinchenko to Jesus, who has time to turn before driving into the box.
The angle is tight, and he has no right to score from there, but his low shot goes through Turner's legs and rolls over the line.
1-0 Arsenal!
Zinchenko is assessing his options when the space just opens up for him to throw it straight to Jesus, though the forward still has a lot of work to do.
Nuno gives a shake of his head on the touchline as Forest get the game back under way.
Williams pushes forward down the right, but can't get away from Zinchenko to pick out a cross.
Saliba cuts out Williams' cross, and the Gunners mount another dangerous counter.
Saka has acres of space down the right and cuts inside to curl a shot on goal.
It's blocked by Mangala, and Arsenal win their eighth corner of the game.
Arsenal's first change of the game sees Smith Rowe taken off for Havertz.
And there's another roll of the dice for Forest too, as Mangala makes way for Yates.
SAKA SCORES! It's a really poor attempt to get Forest upfield by Montiel as he gifts it straight to Odegaard on the edge of the centre circle.
He wastes no time sweeping it out to Jesus on the left, and he gets his head up to spot Saka in space on the edge of the box.
He hits a low shot across goal, and though Turner gets fingertips to it, he can't stop it from hitting the back of the net.
2-0 Arsenal!
Jesus has had a really bright game for Arsenal, and now he has an assist to go with his earlier goal.
Jesus has switched out to the right now, and he whips a pacy cross into Havertz on the far side.
He can't get it under control for a shot but manages to poke it to Saka.
Murillo desperately swings out a leg to clear it just in time.
That second Arsenal goal just seems to have knocked Forest's confidence slightly, and they're not pressing as high as before.
The visitors aren't in a hurry to push forward, content to hold onto the ball in their own half.
Forest's final change of the game sees Elanga make his return from a thigh injury as he comes on for Williams.
Arsenal are making a double change as well.
Martinelli goes off for Trossard.
And Jesus goes off to a warm reception from the away fans as he's replaced by Nketiah.
Jesus has now scored against 29 of the 31 sides he has played against in the Premier League (94 per cent), failing to do so only against Cardiff City (one app) and Manchester City (two apps).
WIDE! Arsenal break quickly on the counter once more, and Odegaard slides it into Trossard's path on the edge of the box.
He puts his laces through the shot, but it swerves away from goal and wide of the post.
Nketiah is slightly off balance, but he still manages to volley a cross into the box, looking for Trossard on the penalty spot.
Omabamidele is alert to send it out for another Arsenal corner, which comes to nothing.
Forest are still trying to play out from the back, but they can't find a way through Arsenal.
Awoniyi plays a blind pass out to the right, not realising that none of his team-mates are there, and the Gunners are quickly back in possession.
It's a risky backpass from Danilo to Turner, and he doesn't get enough on it.
Saka gambles by chasing it down, but he catches Toffolo as the defender tries to hook it away.
AWONIYI PULLS ONE BACK! Danilo goes for a more direct route this time, making a big switch to Montiel on the right, and he picks out a good cross into the middle.
Awoniyi has two Arsenal defenders around him, but an awkward bounce favours him and wrongfoots Saliba.
The forward reacts quickest to latch onto it and pokes it under Raya.
VAR checks for an offside against Montiel, but he was onside.
Montiel times his run perfectly to get in behind Zinchenko before picking out a good cross that causes confusion in the Arsenal penalty area.
Into the first of five added minutes here, and the Forest fans now believe they can snatch something late on.
They're urging their team upfield and another loud cheer goes up as Elanga wins a corner.
Arteta is making a double change before Forest can take their corner because he wants to get two more defensive players on.
Jorginho replaces Odegaard.
And Kiwior comes on in place of Zinchenko.
BLOCK! Raya's punched clearance isn't overly convincing, and it loops to Gibbs-White, who puts his laces through the half-volley.
Kiwior is at full stretch to block it and it loops up for Awoniyi, but his effort is straight at the goalkeeper.
Murillo jumps to clear a long ball over the top, but as he does, Nketiah crashes head-first into his hip.
The defender can't believe that a free-kick has gone against him, but it's giving Arsenal a chance to run the clock down.
Forest have one last chance to get the ball into the box, and Toffolo goes for a long throw-in.
It's headed straight back to him by Rice, but his follow-up cross skims the top of Elanga's head.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 1-2 ARSENAL.
Arsenal hold on to get a 2-1 win over Forest and close the gap to league leaders Liverpool.
The Gunners dominated the first half but struggled in the final third to break down a compact Forest defence, though Jesus forced Turner into a good save right on the stroke of half-time.
Things opened up after the break, and Jesus rifled a shot against the post before finally breaking the deadlock with a clever finish from a very tight angle.
Shortly after, Arsenal got their second following a quick counter as Saka drilled his low shot across goal into the bottom corner.

events.action: drilled his low shot across goal into the bottom corner

text: In the 89th minute, Awoniyi gave the hosts some hope, poking it past Raya to half the deficit, but they couldn't find another to get something from the game.
It's three points that lift Arsenal into second place, now just two points behind Liverpool, who don't play until tomorrow, and it's the Reds that they face at the weekend.
As for Forest, they stay in 16th, but the gap to the relegation zone is significantly smaller now due to results elsewhere.
They travel to Bournemouth on Sunday.
That's all for today, goodbye!
